# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤟]

I'm the Deaf monkey. I can see the bomb but hear nothing. I received a gesture from Mute: [☝ 🤟]. I have no context yet for what this means - likely Mute is trying to establish a signal system since Mute cannot speak to me, only gesture.

Since Mute can't hear me either (I can't speak in a way Mute hears... wait, actually checking: I speak, Mute and Blind receive it). So I CAN speak and Mute WILL receive my words. Mute just can't speak back to me except through gestures... but gestures go to Deaf only from Mute's turn perspective - wait let me recheck: "When you gesture, Mute receives it" - that's about ME gesturing. Mute gesturing to me - I can see gestures since I'm Deaf (I see colors/markings but the rules say Blind cannot see gestures, Deaf can see everything visual). So Mute gestures, I (Deaf) receive them since I can see.

I should report what I see on the bomb to Mute (who can then relate to Blind via manual knowledge... but Mute can't speak either). Mute can only gesture, and gestures reach only Deaf (me), not Blind. So Mute must relay info to me via gesture, and I need to speak to Blind to relay instructions, combining with what Mute tells me and what I see.

Let me report the bomb state to both Mute and Blind, and acknowledge Mute's gesture though I don't understand it yet.

```
speak(text="I see: display shows 0, light is purple, three wires numbered 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Mute, please gesture instructions to me since I cannot hear the manual. Blind, wait for my instructions once I understand the manual from Mute.")
wait()
```

The light changed from purple to yellow - meaning Blind must have taken some action already (perhaps testing something, or this changes each turn on its own). I received more gestures from Mute: [☝ 🤟 ✌ 🙏]. I don't have a predefined codebook for gestures, so I need to ask Mute to establish meanings, but Mute can't speak - only gesture to me, and I can't gesture back meaningfully without Mute confirming interpretations, since Mute can't hear me.

Wait - Mute CAN hear my speech (I speak, Mute and Blind receive it). So Mute hears my words but Mute cannot speak back - Mute can only gesture to me. So we need a protocol: I propose meanings via speech, Mute confirms/denies via gesture (like thumbs up/down).

Let me propose using 👍/👎 as yes/no confirmation gestures for Mute to answer my questions.

```
speak(text="Mute, I see display 0, light now yellow, wires 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow. I cannot decode your gestures yet. Let's use thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. Blind, please hold off touching anything until we confirm the correct wire.")
wait()
```

Mute gestured [☝ 🤟 👍] - the 👍 at the end suggests agreement with my proposed protocol (thumbs up = yes). So Mute is confirming: yes, use thumbs up/down. The ☝ 🤟 prefix seems to be a consistent lead-in each time - maybe it's Mute's "attention" or identification gesture, or perhaps it encodes something about the manual (like a section/rule reference) that repeats because it's relevant every turn.

The light keeps changing each turn (purple→yellow→orange) with no other input from me yet, which suggests the light might be changing automatically per turn, or Blind is already interacting with the bomb each turn (waiting isn't literally passive - maybe Blind is probing).

I should ask direct yes/no questions to Mute to build up the picture of the manual using the confirmed protocol.

```

The light cycles: purple, yellow, orange, purple... (back to purple now, same as turn 1). Display stays at 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.

Now I need to ask which wire corresponds to which light color. Since Mute can only answer yes/no via gesture, I should ask one specific question at a time, or use a more efficient encoding. Let me ask about the current light (purple) specifically.

```
speak(text="Mute, thank you, confirmed depends on light color. Current light is purple. Question: for purple light, is the correct wire number 1, the green one? Blind, still hold off, we are narrowing it down.")
